name: Jiang Weihai
current_role: Co-founder, former director and general manager, Henan Xindaxin Materials (Kaifeng); current role not found
profile: Senior engineer who co-founded Henan Xindaxin Materials, a Kaifeng maker of silicon-carbide slicing powders used to cut solar-grade silicon wafers. Second-largest shareholder (22.56%) and GM at its 2010 ChiNext IPO (300080). The company was later taken over by state-owned Pingmei Shenma and renamed Yicheng New Energy; his current activity is not public.
interesting_fact: Xindaxin's core product was specialised silicon-carbide 'edge material' (刃料) for slicing crystalline-silicon solar wafers; Jiang personally co-developed the dedicated solar-cell wafer-slicing powder project in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: Started in 1982 as a technician at China No.2 Grinding Wheel Factory, served as deputy township head of Yingyang, Dengfeng (1991-93), then ran Zhengzhou White Dove Micro-powder and worked on 20+ White Dove Group R&D projects before joining Xindaxin in 2004.
notes: Hurun 2010 listing. Born Dec 1962 per IPO prospectus. No current public profile or contacts found; Yicheng New Energy (300080.SZ) is now state-controlled, so the old company is not a route to him. MarketScreener lists a 'Wei Hai Jiang' but match unverified.

name: Uday J Desai
current_role: Founder director / managing director, Frost International Ltd (Mumbai commodity trader) per company registry listings
profile: Uday Jayant Desai is listed as founder director and managing director of Frost International Ltd, a Mumbai commodity-trading company (incorporated 1995, also with a Kanpur presence) that traded a large portfolio of agri and other commodities. Hurun ranked him in 2017-18. Registry sites show the company under insolvency resolution (CIRP) as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Frost International traded a broad commodity portfolio out of Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex and Kanpur; company material credits Uday J. Desai as founder director who grew its trade volumes.
notes: Thin, aggregator-only sourcing; identity only partly confirmed. Company reportedly in insolvency (CIRP) per IBBI listing https://ibbi.gov.in/claims/pub-process/U05001MH1995PLC243081 - likely no longer UHNW; low-priority outreach target. No published contacts found.

name: Mahendra Nahata
current_role: Promoter & Managing Director, HFCL Ltd; director, Reliance Jio Infocomm
profile: Kolkata-raised B.Com (St. Xavier's) who co-promoted Himachal Futuristic Communications (HFCL) in 1987, building it from transmission equipment into a telecom gear, optical-fibre and defence-electronics maker. MD since 2005 and on the Jio Infocomm board; in 2026 he is pushing HFCL's record order book and calling for Indian data-centre and R&D expansion.
interesting_fact: Voice & Data named him 'Telecom Man of the Millennium' in 2003; he also has been president of the Telecom Equipment Manufacturers Association of India, and his family holds a stake in Jio Platforms.
deep_cut_fact: Before telecom, he began his business career dabbling in tea trading out of New Jalpaiguri, a small town in north Bengal.
notes: Strong podcast fit: publicly advocating data-centre and telecom-infrastructure build-out (Entrepreneur India 2026: https://india.entrepreneur.com/business-news/entrepreneur-2026-hfcls-mahendra-nahata-calls-for-infra-data-centre-expansion-and-rd-investment). Son Anant Nahata runs Exicom (EV chargers/telecom power). Route via HFCL company secretary/IR.

name: Hu Jishen
current_role: Chairman of the board, Xingyue Group (Yongkang, Zhejiang) per brand-profile site; date unverified
profile: Founder figure of Xingyue (Star Moon) Group in Yongkang, Zhejiang, which grew from a small workshop into a diversified manufacturer of power equipment/engines, doors and tools, reportedly with 4,000+ staff and a place among China's top 500 private firms. Hurun listed him (with Hu Jirong) in 2005-07. Current activity not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Xingyue grew from a factory with annual output under RMB 1 million into a group with over RMB 2 billion in assets, spanning engines, doors and hardware tools in Yongkang, China's 'hardware capital'.
deep_cut_fact: He served about 20 years as Party secretary of Gushan village in Gushan town, Yongkang, and reportedly put around RMB 30 million into the village's infrastructure; he was also vice-chair of the Jinhua federation of industry and commerce.
notes: Only source is a promotional brand-directory profile (CNPP); verify before use. Shares the Hurun listing with Hu Jirong (relationship not confirmed). No published contacts found.

name: Gerold Buettiker
current_role: Chairman, Gebuka AG (Swiss investment company); ~13% holder of Aebi Schmidt Holding AG (Nasdaq: AEBI)
profile: Swiss industrialist/investor (ETH undergraduate, University of Zurich doctorate) who holds his stake in specialty-vehicle maker Aebi Schmidt through his wholly owned Gebuka AG. He sat on Aebi Schmidt's supervisory board before its 2025 merger with The Shyft Group and Nasdaq listing, and has held board seats at Swiss Steel Holding, Deutsche Edelstahlwerke and Nueva Holding.
interesting_fact: After Aebi Schmidt merged with US truck-body maker Shyft Group in 2025 and listed on Nasdaq, Büttiker emerged as one of its two major shareholders with about 13%.
notes: Very low public profile; stake held via Gebuka AG (Neuheim, Switzerland) per Schedule 13G https://www.secform4.com/13dg/2081403/0001214659-25-012273.html. Board roles from MarketScreener aggregator. No published personal/office contact; Aebi Schmidt IR would be the only corporate route.

name: C Sathyan
current_role: Vice Chairman, Hatsun Agro Product Ltd (Chennai)
profile: Son of founder R.G. Chandramogan, C. (Chandramogan) Sathyan became executive director of Hatsun Agro in 2002, later MD and since 2024 (Executive) Vice Chairman, supporting the chairman on strategy. Hatsun is India's largest private dairy (Arun Ice Creams, Arokya milk, Hatsun curd, Ibaco), buying milk from 400,000+ farmers across South India.
interesting_fact: Hatsun began in 1970 as a single Arun ice-cream shed in Chennai started with Rs 13,000 and now procures millions of litres of milk a day; it famously earns more in minutes today than in its first decade.
notes: Signed filings as Vice Chairman in March 2026, so active. Little personal press; father R.G. Chandramogan is the public face. Best route is Hatsun's corporate office.

name: Rudra Chatterjee
current_role: Managing Director, Luxmi Group (Luxmi Tea / Luxmi Estates); Chairman, Obeetee Carpets; Chairman, Silverback Tea
profile: Kolkata businessman who has run century-old Luxmi Tea (MD since 2007), producing ~30 million kg of tea from about 25 estates in India and Africa and owning the Makaibari Darjeeling brand. He also chairs Obeetee, India's historic hand-knotted carpet maker, and is pushing Luxmi (rebranded Luxmi Estates) into global direct-to-consumer tea.
interesting_fact: Under him Makaibari made a special-edition tea for King Charles III's coronation and hosted a G20 event at the estate, while Obeetee supplied carpets for India's new Parliament building and Rashtrapati Bhavan.
deep_cut_fact: Asked about the big projects, he deflected credit: he said he may be part of it but is not all of it - many other members are pulling it.
notes: Media-friendly: speaks at tea conventions and gives interviews (Telegraph t2, tea-biz). Route via Luxmi Estates / Makaibari corporate comms; no published email found in this pass.
